answer: The ripple graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the horizon audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 4 times its size, so a group of 84 keys loses far more than 84 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the quill checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 18 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
